# MM-P1-L4-HP02 - Maintenance manual - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2
Revision: Rev B
Plant: P1, line P1-L4
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Scope
This manual covers planned and reactive maintenance activities for the Heat Treat hydraulic forging press identified as EQ-P1-L4-HP02 in line P1-L4. It defines approved tools, safety controls, stepwise procedures for mechanical and hydraulic maintenance actions, acceptance criteria for returned-to-service condition, and recordkeeping expectations. This manual is intended for qualified maintenance technicians trained on press systems and controls and operating under the plant maintenance policy. Refer to SOP-P1-L4-01, SOP-P1-L4-02, and SOP-P1-L4-03 for operational procedures and lockout/tagout requirements.

Background and rationale
The hydraulic forging press is a high-energy mechanical system where fastener integrity and hydraulic pressure management are critical for safe operation and product quality. Main ram retention hardware and system pressure controls are key failure modes. The main ram bolt is the primary restraint for the ram assembly; its clamping preload must be verified and maintained to ensure alignment and prevent progressive loosening that can lead to catastrophic component separation. The hydraulic system pressure limit is set to protect seals, hoses, and pressure vessels while maintaining forging capability. Adhering to specified bolt clamping and pressure limits preserves press life and reduces unplanned downtime.

Tools and materials
- Calibrated torque wrench capable of achieving the specified main ram bolt torque.
- Hydraulic system pressure gauge calibrated to plant standards for verification against the system pressure limit.
- Manufacturer-approved fastener retention compound where required by OEM procedures.
- Clean rags, appropriate lifting and support stands, and non-marring drift tools for component alignment.
- Lockout/tagout kit and personal protective equipment per SOP-P1-L4-02.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Coordinate with production and maintenance supervision to schedule the work window and confirm isolation of press electrical and hydraulic sources per SOP-P1-L4-02.
- Apply lockout/tagout and verify zero energy state on the press. Confirm notification of affected operators per SOP-P1-L4-01.
- Inspect the work area for hazards and ensure suitable lighting and access. Assemble tools and verify calibration certificates for torque and pressure instruments.

Main ram bolt verification and torque application
- Support the ram assembly to remove axial load from the main ram bolt before any measurement or torque application. Use only suitable mechanical supports and stands rated for the assembly weight.
- Clean bolt threads and clamping surfaces to remove corrosion, debris, and old compound. If the OEM indicates a retention compound is required, apply manufacturer-approved compound sparingly to the threads per product datasheet.
- Using the calibrated torque wrench, set the wrench to the main ram bolt torque specified for EQ-P1-L4-HP02. The main ram bolt torque for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 970 N·m.
- Apply torque in controlled increments to achieve final specified torque. If multiple torquing passes are recommended by the OEM, follow their sequence while maintaining alignment of the ram assembly.
- After torquing, inspect the bolt and surrounding components for proper seating and absence of distortion or damage.

Hydraulic system pressure verification
- With mechanical work complete and supports verified, remove isolation devices per SOP-P1-L4-02 and slowly reintroduce hydraulic supply while monitoring for leaks and abnormal noise.
- Use the calibrated pressure gauge to confirm that no pressure source exceeds the system pressure limit for this press. The system pressure limit for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 300 bar.
- If any component forces system pressure above the specified limit during normal operation or test cycles, cease operation and follow fault isolation procedures in SOP-P1-L4-03.

Functional checks and run-in
- Perform controlled operational cycles at low actuator demand to confirm proper ram guidance, smooth travel, and absence of binding. Observe hydraulic manifold for leaks or pressure spikes and listen for unusual sounds.
- Validate safety interlocks and emergency stop functions per SOP-P1-L4-01 before returning the press to production.

Examples and diagnostic notes
- Example condition: observable thread damage on main ram bolt. Rationale: damaged threads cannot reliably retain required preload; replace bolt per OEM parts guidance and re-torque to the specified value after installation and verification of thread integrity.
- Example condition: transient pressure spike observed during initial run-in that approaches the specified limit. Rationale: spikes near the system limit may indicate relief valve drift, blocked return, or actuator binding. Isolate hydraulic circuit, drain to safe condition, and inspect relief valves and actuator seals per SOP-P1-L4-03.

Acceptance criteria
- Mechanical: main ram bolt is torqued to the specified value and shows no signs of thread stripping, head rounding, or component distortion. Fastener seating surfaces are clean and secure.
- Hydraulic: system pressure during static and dynamic checks does not exceed the system pressure limit and operates smoothly without uncontained fluid leaks.
- Functional: press completes operational checks with safety interlocks functioning and no abnormal vibration, noise, or thermal anomalies noted during run-in.
- Records: all inspection results, torque wrench calibration references, pressure gauge calibration references, part replacement notes, and signatures of performing and verifying technicians must be recorded. Include date and reference to this document id and revision.

Records to keep
- Work order or maintenance ticket referencing this manual id MM-P1-L4-HP02 and revision Rev B.
- Torque application log showing the instrument ID and calibration reference used when applying the main ram bolt torque.
- Hydraulic pressure verification log showing the pressure instrument ID and calibration reference used when confirming the system pressure limit.
- Photographic evidence of bolt condition and torque marking where applicable, and any replacement fastener or component serial traces.
- Incident or deviation report if acceptance criteria are not met, including corrective action and re-verification notes.

Related documents
- SOP-P1-L4-01
- SOP-P1-L4-02
- SOP-P1-L4-03

Revision control
Maintain this document in the controlled document system. Update only through the approved document change process and reference change justification when revising.
